newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity end higher on SW heat, natgas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity end higher on SW heat, natgas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures traded higher amid forecasts of above-normal temperatures in the U.S. Southwest, strong natural gas prices, and continued cool weather at high elevations in the Pacific Northwest, traders said Wednesday.
"This market has rallied considerably over the past couple of weeks because of colder temperatures in the mountains. That trend is continuing," said one dealer.
The weather conditions have slowed inflows into hydroelectric projects at the same time spill requirements began at some dams as an aid to annual fish migration.
Traders also cited hot weather in parts of the Southwest, which will spur some air-conditioning demand, as contributing to the bullish tone for the electricity futures complex.
Forecasts called for Southwest temperatures as much as 12 degrees F above normal through Sunday, easing to slightly above normal for the six to 10-day outlook.
The Northwest was expected to see temperatures three to nine degrees above normal through Sunday, and near normal to above normal for the 6 to 10-day timeframe.

In addition, strong natural gas prices were said to be adding to the upward trend for electricity, with May NYMEX Henry Hub settling up 6.8 cents at $2.005 per million British thermal units on Wednesday.
The May Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures contract settled up 56 cents at $16.35 a megawatt hour (MWh), while June finished 57 cents higher at $17.50.
May California Oregon Border (COB) ended up 38 cents at $12.99 after trading as low as $12.80, while June was up 26 cents at $12.55.
NYMEX estimated 385 COB and 725 PV contracts were sold.
